subject.title: [Feature]: Add JSON-RPC bindings for language-agnostic plugins

question: Should OpenClaw accept JSON-RPC stdio child-process bindings as a supported public plugin manifest and SDK ABI for language-agnostic plugins?
rationale: The request adds a new public plugin API and process trust boundary; current code does not already solve it, and the linked draft PR is an implementation candidate rather than a settled product decision.

options.title: Review and accept the linked PR
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98005 as the canonical implementation path and require explicit maintainer acceptance of protocol v1, host permissions, lifecycle, and support expectations before merge.

options.title: Narrow or gate the ABI
options.body: Keep the feature open but reduce the supported registration or host-call surface until the compatibility and security boundary are smaller.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Leave the issue as a product-design record if maintainers are not ready to own a language-neutral child-process plugin ABI.

recommendation.title: Review and accept the linked PR
recommendation.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98005 as the canonical implementation path and require explicit maintainer acceptance of protocol v1, host permissions, lifecycle, and support expectations before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent manifest and SDK boundary history makes this the best available owner signal for deciding the public plugin ABI direction.
